judged_text: The handler trusts the parent's raw numeric userId to identify the local user (the schema comment says 'UserId of the cal.com user') with no cross-instance identity mapping or verification such as an email check. Unless the child instance's user id space is kept identical to cal.com's, the webhook delivers one cal.com user's OAuth credentials to the local user holding the same numeric id — a different person — who then books meetings through another user's calendar; any user created or deleted on either side diverges the id spaces and nothing in the design detects it.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added webhook handler `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the request schema requires a raw numeric `userId` and the handler directly looks up and writes credentials by that local `id` (`prisma.user.findUnique({ where: { id: reqBody.userId } })` and then `prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { userId: reqBody.userId, ... } })`). There is no cross-instance identity verification (e.g., email/UUID mapping) or any check that the `userId` refers to the same person across systems. If the sending system’s user ID space differs from the receiving instance’s, credentials could be created/updated for the wrong local user who happens to share that numeric ID, which is a real security/correctness risk grounded in this diff.
